Use-case: stylized-concept. Production game equipment sprite sheet for an existing Korean portrait pixel-art hack-and-slash RPG. Use the reference ONLY for its crisp detailed pixel-art style and weapon orientation; author a substantially new silhouette, not a recolor. A wide transparent canvas with exactly three separated equal-width columns in ONE horizontal row: sword at left, wearable chest armor at center, hanging magical charm at right. Only these three isolated objects, no text, no labels, no character, no hands, no background, no floor, no checkerboard baked in. Each object entirely inside its cell with generous transparent margins. Sharp dark outline, limited bright specular pixels, earthy shadow pixels, clearly readable at small game size. Sword must run diagonally from a distinct grip and pommel at lower left to a tip at upper right (roughly 55 degrees above horizontal), blade pointing NE exactly like reference, no detached blade. Armor is an empty front-view wearable torso and pauldrons with a clear neck opening, no head, no arms, no legs; practical slightly tapered waist. Charm is a pendant with a small top hanging loop. No glow halo pixels bleeding outside an object's cell; contained emissive detail is okay. Grade: EXTREMELY RARE, highest tier. White platinum, champagne gold with restrained prismatic teal/purple/red glints. Sword: a constellation blade with a single pointed crystalline core and short floating-looking but structurally connected star-shaped side fins along its spine, elegant wide winged crossguard and distinct dark grip at lower left, tip NE. Armor: white platinum breastplate, broad symmetrical star-ray pauldrons, narrow articulated waist and luminous star-shaped chest core; unmistakably more elaborate than the other three grades without covering a character's head. Charm: a radiant eight-point star in a broken circular halo cage with a top hanging loop.
